newsitem.title: USA: ABA, IBAA say will sue over U.S. farm lending rule.
newsitem.headline: ABA, IBAA say will sue over U.S. farm lending rule.

text.p: The American Bankers Association and the Independent Bankers Association of America announced Tuesday they would sue federal regulators to prevent an expansion of Farm Credit System lending.

Suit would be filed, a spokesman said, at about the time a new "customer eligibility" rule took effect. The rule, proposed by the Farm Credit Administration, was expected to become final in mid-March.
In a statement, the two trade groups for bankers said the new rule would allow Farm Credit System members to expand the scope of their lending without legal authority.
Banks provide about 40 percent of lending for the farm sector and the Farm Credit System provides 25 percent.
The new rule would allow Farm Credit System members to support farm-related services. FCA oversees the FCS.

"Congress gave the FCS a subsidy in 1916 to serve a specific market, namely the farmer, and they should stick to that market," said Bill McQuillan, IBAA president-elect and president of a bank in Greeley, Nebraska.
FCA leaders were not immediately for comment. In recent congressional testimony, they said the rule was "merely a badly needed update."
